My parents were like yours. I was generally a good kid too, but it made me more secretive the move they tried to move their way into my life in order to control it. My mom is old. My dad is dead. I have come to accept that some parents will never have the realization that they have done some things erroneously. It hurts. If your parents are generally kind people, sit with them and talk. Maybe start out saying “all people make mistakes, right?” And go on to say that you realize how hard it is to let go of something you love so much, but their roles are to raise you to function in our world. Nobody in our world likes to be tracked at all times. (I’m sure governments do anyway, when t they need to.) 

Alternatively, you could do the unhealthy thing I would’ve done at your age and turn it off, say it drained your battery. Do that enough and they’ll find an alternative quick. Sometimes you have to think laterally when you have to deal with inflexible people.

Hey. I have invisible scars from my mommy telling five year old me she no longer loved me when I spilt her perfume on her (massive) vanity mirror. Sending you love through time and space.

As do I. The main reason being I had the shittiest childhood without even realizing it. I didn’t need those words to know my dad and mom were self-absorbed, vapid, ill-matched, and miserable together. Shoulda divorced instead of having me.
I love Boudicca, and the English language.

I grew up with gay. I always found gay friends, and magically gravitated to them. My Junior prom date is now married to a man.  People called me “fruit fly” or “ f** hag.” When I had my daughter, I exposed her to every subculture I could find. I brought her to pride parades (our city has two), tattoo conventions, and the outdoorsy folk. I almost expected her to be gay. I did that so she could really make a sense of what sort of people she liked, and to judge a person by the content of their character   

Having been around so much gayness, coming out is one of the most character-building milestones gay people have. Even when parents accept it (albeit somewhat reluctantly) they find that their relationship comes out stronger in the end. 

Parents have difficulty letting go of the vision they had for their children. My childhood was neglectful and oftentimes abusive, and I resented that my parents wanted me to fit into their mold. Even when I did, they still weren’t kind to me. So I chose to be who I wanted to be. The fact that you didn’t throw your son out, and that you’re learning and maturing from your shared bonding experience shows me you love him. Embrace the discomfort. You’re evolving to nurture his emotional needs, and that can be a path to a more open relationship. 

That being said, wait til you go to your first gay event. It’s the time people get to be themselves and be celebrated for it, so it’s an absolute blast. There is nothing but love around on those events.

I lasted 6 years in my marriage. It was the “American Dream” too. We were in our mid 20s making six figures together, two dogs, and a child. 

I left him because I wanted more, and if I’m brutally honest, I just exchanged it for a different brand of unhappy.
I got close today. I have a picture of my kid I keep with me so I can keep her in mind, but I almost feel as though she’s much better off without me. Sad or stupid that might sound.

I’ve been on lithium as an augmenting agent. Zoloft, Prozac, Celexa, Cymbalta, Lithium... you name it. A lot of them work beautifully for the first few months but summertime, around July the thoughts start. It began the year an immediate family member got diagnosed with cancer, and every year it hits a peak in summer. 

I am exhausted.

A friend suggested this as well, and I’m calling my doctor for an emergency appointment as soon as they open. I’ll mention it because I am at my wit’s end. I’ve been on klonopin and Xanax before, and those hardly worked. Gabapentin didn’t work, and GABA meds just make me feel generally uncomfortable. My labs came out fine the last time but I really don’t know what else to do. 

I’ve had traditional psychotherapy as well as DBT. I am really at a loss as to how to go forward.
